description: Regulatory summaries, not legal advice. Public, well-documented sender-ID and alphanumeric-registration regimes for 40 countries. Compiled for https://smsroute-cc.github.io/tools/sender-id-rules-by-country.html; deeper background at https://smsroute.cc/blog/sms-sender-id-by-country-rules.

rows.notes: US carriers do not deliver alphanumeric sender IDs; brands register a 10DLC campaign or use a toll-free/short code instead.
rows.basis: per CTIA messaging principles / carrier A2P 10DLC framework

rows.notes: Alphanumeric sender IDs are not reliably delivered; A2P traffic typically runs over long codes or short codes instead.
rows.basis: per Canadian carrier A2P messaging practice

rows.notes: Alphanumeric sender IDs are widely used; no centralized government pre-registration beyond normal carrier/aggregator onboarding.
rows.basis: per UK mobile network operator practice

rows.notes: Alphanumeric sender IDs are commonly used by businesses with no centralized registry.
rows.basis: per German mobile network operator practice

rows.notes: Alphanumeric sender IDs are widely used; no centralized government registry for the sender ID itself.

rows.notes: Alphanumeric sender IDs must be registered with local operators before use; unregistered senders are commonly blocked.
rows.basis: per UAE TRA / telecom operator sender ID registration requirement

rows.notes: Alphanumeric sender IDs require pre-registration with local operators; unregistered senders are commonly blocked or overridden.
rows.basis: per CITC Saudi Arabia sender ID registration requirement

rows.notes: Alphanumeric sender IDs generally require registration with local operators, following the wider GCC pre-registration pattern.
rows.basis: per Qatar telecom operator sender ID registration practice

rows.notes: Marketing messages require İYS (electronic message management system) consent records plus an operator-level sender title (başlık) registration.
rows.basis: per BTK / İYS Turkey electronic messaging regulation

rows.notes: Sender numbers/IDs used for bulk messaging must be pre-registered; KISA operates the sender number verification system used by carriers.
rows.basis: per KISA sender number pre-registration requirement

rows.notes: Japanese carriers commonly override or restrict custom alphanumeric sender display; numeric and short-code routes are the standard path.
rows.basis: per Japanese mobile carrier SMS delivery practice

rows.notes: Sender headers and content templates must be registered on the DLT (Distributed Ledger Technology) platform via a TRAI-registered telecom operator before sending.
rows.basis: per TRAI DLT regulation for commercial SMS

rows.notes: Alphanumeric sender IDs must be registered in the SMS Sender ID Registry (SSIR); unregistered alphanumeric senders are labeled 'Likely-SCAM' by default.
rows.basis: per Singapore SMS Sender ID Registry (SSIR) requirement

rows.notes: Alphanumeric sender IDs generally require registration with local operators/regulator before delivery.
rows.basis: per Malaysian telecom operator sender ID registration practice

rows.notes: Alphanumeric sender IDs are commonly used; some operators require additional registration for masking/bank-grade sender names.
rows.basis: per Philippine mobile operator practice

rows.notes: Alphanumeric 'brandname' sender IDs require pre-registration with local telecom operators, typically backed by a business license.
rows.basis: per Vietnam telecom operator brandname registration requirement

rows.notes: Sender IDs must be registered with the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) via a local aggregator before use.
rows.basis: per NCC Nigeria sender ID registration requirement

rows.notes: Alphanumeric sender IDs are commonly used without a centralized government sender-ID registry.
rows.basis: per South African mobile operator practice

rows.notes: Alphanumeric sender IDs are generally allowed; higher-volume A2P traffic typically goes through local aggregator approval.
rows.basis: per Brazilian mobile operator A2P practice

rows.notes: Alphanumeric sender IDs are commonly used without a centralized government sender-ID registry.
rows.basis: per Mexican mobile operator practice

rows.notes: Australia is rolling out an industry-run SMS Sender ID Registration program (ACMA-backed) so brands register alphanumeric IDs to curb spoofing; unregistered alphanumeric senders face growing restrictions.
rows.basis: per ACMA / Australian mobile carrier SMS Sender ID Registration Program

rows.notes: Alphanumeric sender IDs are commonly used without a centralized government sender-ID registry.
rows.basis: per New Zealand mobile operator practice

rows.notes: Sender IDs generally require regulator/operator approval before commercial use.
rows.basis: per NTRA Egypt sender ID registration practice

rows.notes: Commercial sender IDs (headlines) must be registered with operators under PTA anti-spam rules before sending.
rows.basis: per PTA Pakistan SMS headline (sender ID) registration requirement

rows.notes: Alphanumeric sender names require registration tied to a legal entity, arranged through a licensed local aggregator.
rows.basis: per Russian mobile operator alphanumeric name registration requirement

rows.notes: Alphanumeric sender IDs are commonly used without a centralized government sender-ID registry.
rows.basis: per Hong Kong mobile operator practice
